function.name: get_current_time
function.description: Get the current local date and time

function.name: get_uptime
function.description: Report system uptime, logged-in user count, and the 1/5/15-minute load averages. Use for any question about system load, how busy the machine is, or how long it has been running.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read and return the full contents of a file at the given path.

path.description: Absolute or relative path to the file to read

function.name: write_file
function.description: Write content to a file at the given path, creating it if it doesn't exist and overwriting it if it does.

path.description: Absolute or relative path to the file to write

content.description: Text content to write to the file

function.name: apply_patch
function.description:
Apply a patch to files on disk using the V4A "*** Begin Patch" patch format. Prefer this over write_file when you are changing a few lines of a large file: you send only the changed lines instead of re-emitting the whole file. The `patch` argument is the complete patch text, for example:
*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: /opt/strategies/clone_abc123/main.py
@@
-from price_feed import get_price
+from price_feed import get_price
+from moving_averages import exponential_moving_average as ema
*** End Patch
Every line inside an @@ hunk must start with '-' (a line to remove), '+' (a line to add) or a space (an unchanged line of context). The '-' and context lines must match the file EXACTLY as it is on disk right now, so read_file the target first and copy the lines from it. A hunk that matches nothing, or that matches in more than one place, aborts the ENTIRE patch and writes nothing -- include enough surrounding context to be unambiguous. Also supports '*** Add File: <path>' (body is all '+' lines), '*** Delete File: <path>' and '*** Move to: <path>'. Relative paths resolve against the current working directory; absolute paths are safer. If a patch will not match after a retry, fall back to write_file with the complete new file contents.

patch.description: The complete patch text, from '*** Begin Patch' through '*** End Patch'

function.name: fetch_url
function.description: Fetch the contents of a URL via curl (follows redirects) and return the response body.

url.description: The URL to fetch, e.g. https://example.com

function.name: install_package
function.description: Install a package via apt-get (apt-get install -y <package>).

package.description: The apt package name to install, e.g. jq

function.name: update_package_list
function.description: Refresh the apt package index (apt-get update). Run this before installing a package if it might not be found.

function.name: exec
function.description: Execute a shell command via `/bin/sh -c <command>` and return its combined stdout/stderr. Use for anything not covered by a more specific tool (e.g. process management, piping, shell built-ins). Not sandboxed beyond the container itself, so avoid destructive commands.

command.description: The shell command to run, e.g. "ls -la /opt"

function.name: recall
function.description: Look up a single previously remembered fact by its key. Most remembered facts are already included in the system prompt automatically; use this only to check a specific key or after list_memories.

key.description: The key previously used with remember

function.name: forget
function.description: Delete a previously remembered fact by key so it stops being loaded into future runs.

key.description: The key previously used with remember

function.name: list_memories
function.description: List every remembered key and its value.
